subject: Patent backstop: proposed MSA carve-out and escrow/insurance coordination

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the quick turn. We attached our redlines; the only open legal on our side that will block signature is the liability cap carve-out for IP indemnity. Given the product will be embedded into safety-critical devices on our robots, our security and IP teams need stronger protection for third-party patent assertions.

High-level ask: we need IP indemnity (patent & copyright claims arising from Redwood-delivered model outputs or model weights) to be excluded from the monetary liability cap (or, alternatively, to have a separate unlimited indemnity for IP) OR to have a backstop mechanism that is operationally equivalent (escrow + insurance).

If Redwood won't remove IP from the cap entirely, we propose the following compromise:
- Redwood retains the overall liability cap for non-IP claims;
- IP indemnity remains outside the monetary cap but only for direct costs of defense, settlements, and awarded damages that arise from third-party IP claims;
- As a mitigation, Redwood deposits a copy of the model weights and a small escrow [see attached proposed_escrow_terms] and provides evidence of an active insurance policy (COI) that names Acme as an additional insured, with reasonable limits (we propose $5M per occurrence).

We know this is a material ask, but without it our internal procurement cannot sign. Let us know what minimal, operational changes Redwood would accept to close this. We are trying to keep timeline to end of next week.

—Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Contracts, Acme Robotics

Vanessa / team —

Thanks for the ping. We can offer a compromise that is defensible for Sales and acceptable commercially. Proposed approach below (redline language sketch + operational asks). I put a clean copy and the escrow template in attachments.

1) Redline sketch (to propose back to Acme):
"Notwithstanding Section 10 (Limitation of Liability), the aggregate liability cap set forth therein shall not apply to Vendor’s indemnification obligations for third-party claims alleging infringement of patents or copyrights arising solely from Vendor-provided model weights, binaries, or other materials delivered under this Agreement (\"Vendor IP Claims\"). For avoidance of doubt, this carve-out does not apply to claims arising out of (a) Customer’s modification of the deliverables, (b) Customer prompt content supplied by Customer, or (c) integration/custom code authored by Customer. Vendor’s indemnity obligation for Vendor IP Claims shall be limited to defense costs, settlements and final adjudicated damages attributable to the Vendor IP Claim, unless otherwise prohibited by applicable law."

Rationale: this keeps the carve-out narrow to Redwood-originated deliverables and preserves general exposure limits for other categories. It gives Acme a meaningful indemnity for core IP while containing runaway exposure.

2) Operational mitigations (what we provide):
- Escrow: We are willing to place a non-production copy of the model weights and associated reproducible build info in escrow under commercially reasonable terms; escrow access shall require (i) written notice of an asserted Vendor IP Claim and (ii) final judgment or failure to obtain a license within a commercially reasonable cure period (we propose 120 days). Escrow agent to be mutually agreed.
- Insurance: We will provide evidence of existing IP/legal liability insurance (COI) with limits of $3M per occurrence / $6M aggregate. If Acme insists on higher limits, we can explore increased coverage but will need underwriter approval and time. COI attached.
- Timelines: We can accept a short-term signature if Acme signs a SOW that includes a remediation timeline (e.g., 60–120 days) to finalize escrow/insurance paperwork post-signature.

3) Notes on negotiation points we should expect:
- Acme will push for unlimited money damages for IP; pushback: unlimited exposure is commercially untenable and would set a bad precedent. Our carve-out is a reasonable middle ground.
- Customer may ask for immediate escrow access on notice — we should insist on either final judgment or failure-to-license after cure (standard pattern).
- If Acme demands additional insured status on our policy, routing through umbrella or an endorsement will be necessary; underwriting timelines could delay close.

Next steps: Vanessa, if you want, I can send this wording to Acme legal with the attached escrow template and COI. Karthik, flag if you want any contract law tweaks; Ben, FYI on the COI limits — any commercial pushes?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick, pragmatic response. The redline sketch looks like a workable path for us. Two operational questions before we route to procurement for final sign: 
1) Escrow trigger: we accept the proposed model (notice + judgment/failure-to-license after cure), but can you compress the cure window to 90 days? Our engineers are time-sensitive.
2) Insurance limits: $3M/$6M is lower than our initial ask; can you confirm whether Redwood is willing to pursue a short-term endorsement to raise the per-occurrence limit to $5M if underwriters permit? If not, procurement will likely ask for a residual escrow amount equal to the shortfall.

If we can get confirmation (or a commit-to-apply-for endorsement) by end of Monday, procurement will move to signature. Otherwise they will require the residual escrow bridge before signature.

I'll expect your confirm and any final escrow agent suggestions.

—Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Contracts, Acme Robotics
thread_summary: Negotiation between Redwood (Vanessa, legal) and Acme (Jordan) on carving IP indemnity out of liability cap. Acme asked for either an uncapped IP indemnity or escrow+insurance backstop. Redwood proposed narrow carve-out limited to vendor-provided model deliverables, offered escrow with 120-day cure and COI at $3M/$6M, and allowed short-term signature with remediation timeline. Acme requested shorter cure (90 days) and potential insurance endorsement up to $5M or residual escrow. Next step: legal to confirm endorsement process and finalize escrow agent/terms.
